scripts.check:specs: openspec validate --all --strict; validated=$?; if grep -rE '^TBD - created by archiving' openspec/specs/ --include='*.md' -l 2>/dev/null; then echo 'ERROR: master specs contain post-archive TBD placeholders at line start. Complete the Purpose section before merging.' >&2; exit 1; fi; if grep -rE '^(## )?Purpose: TBD' openspec/specs/ --include='*.md' -l 2>/dev/null; then echo 'ERROR: master specs contain Purpose: TBD. Complete the Purpose section before merging.' >&2; exit 1; fi; [ $validated -eq 0 ] || exit $validated; echo 'check:specs OK'
scripts.comment:verify: Everything CI runs that can run locally, in one command. It exists because there was no way to run CI's set: `typecheck` is web only and `typecheck:mobile` is mobile only, the packages had no root script at all, and the duplicate-runtime check lived as shell inside the workflow — so a PR could tick the checklist honestly and still fail on a step no local script covered. That happened. Add any new CI step here as well as to the workflow. Order matters: the checks that answer in milliseconds run first, so a missing font or a returning `explore` fails in seconds instead of after a four-minute build. The ONE step this does not cover is `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, left out because verifying should not prune your node_modules: run it yourself when you touch dependencies.
scripts.verify: pnpm check:cycles && pnpm check:openspec-workflows && pnpm check:unarchived && pnpm check:duplicate-deps && pnpm check:fonts && pnpm check:tokens && pnpm check:icons && pnpm check:rls && pnpm exec openspec doctor && pnpm check:specs && pnpm lint && pnpm lint:mobile && pnpm typecheck && pnpm typecheck:mobile && pnpm typecheck:packages && pnpm test && pnpm build
